R0072.title: Employee Corruption
R0072.definition: Employee corruption refers to employees using improper means to seek personal gain, abuse their authority, accept bribes, or engage in corrupt activities in the workplace.
R0072.description: This may include falsifying expense reports, soliciting kickbacks from suppliers, misusing company resources, bribery, or participating in other corrupt activities.
R0072.influence: Employee corruption harms include damaging the company's reputation, undermining internal trust, reducing work efficiency, causing resource waste, increasing compliance risks, and ultimately potentially triggering legal liability and financial losses.

observables: Employee accounts anomalously access financial, procurement, or supplier data unrelated to their duties
Expense reports frequently show suspicious patterns such as amounts just below approval thresholds or frequent changes to supplier information
Fund flows or interest ties between employees and specific suppliers are exposed during audits
Critical business approvals bypass established processes or concentrate in the hands of specific employees

R0072-001.title: Insider-Outsider Collusion
R0072-001.definition: Internal employees collude with external individuals or organizations to commit fraud, embezzlement, bribery, or other improper acts that violate the company's interests and regulations.
R0072-001.description: Behaviors or scenarios include employees colluding with suppliers to falsify expenses, corrupt transactions, and insider-outsider collusion for fraudulent activities.
R0072-001.influence: May cause financial losses and reputational damage to the company, while increasing compliance risks and posing a serious threat to the company's sound operations.

observables: Internal employees have abnormal communication records or fund flows with external suppliers or competitors
Employees anomalously export or exfiltrate sensitive data such as supplier contracts, quotes, or customer information
Procurement or bidding processes show suspicious operations directed toward specific external suppliers
Employee accounts access core business data unrelated to their duties outside of working hours
